We need carefully analyze each story relative to all others. Criterion set-level: a user story is not inconsistent with another. So a story can violate if it conflicts with at least one other story.

Need identify conflicts in backlog.

Let's list stories and possible conflicts:

Roles: anonymoususer, authenticateduser, attendee, trainee, trainer, trainingcoordinator, administrator, sponsor, summit coordinator. Some may be roles via Drupal.

Stories may conflict:
BC-005: As trainer, I want to edit my training node myself. BC-013: trainers can see all class attendance info. No conflict.
BC-006: As trainee, limit to one registration per day per authenticated user. BC-008: attendee added to training waitlist. Maybe registration vs waitlist not conflict. BC-038 summit registration. fine.
BC-009: must accept cancellation terms with checkbox. BC-010 cancellation deadline. fine.
BC-011 add to "my schedule" if schedule feature exists. BC-012 see trainings signed up. fine.
BC-015 and BC-016: training class page vs training options listing. Similar but not conflict.
BC-020: admin refund sponsorship money processed via stripe. BC-021/023/027/030 payment sponsorships. fine.
BC-022: anonymoususer see list attendees associated with company. Potential privacy conflict? BC-013 trainers see all class attendance; BC-014 admin view trainee info; BC-022 anonymous see attendees associated with company? Could conflict with privacy constraints? Not explicit. BC-002: anonymoususer view list of user profiles. Maybe seeing attendees associated with company could reveal user profiles. However no explicit prohibition.
BC-028: admin assign sponsors to events, trainings summits. BC-037 sponsor sponsor summit. Potential conflict? Admin assigns vs sponsor self-sponsors? But not incompatible maybe both.
BC-030/027/021/023 individual sponsorship payment flows. Could conflict with BC-066 choices. Need examine.
BC-040: attendee see summits signed up for prevent double-booking with training or summit. It says prevent double-booking, but no rule preventing double-booking? Could conflict with BC-006 (one registration per day per authenticated user). "prevent myself from accidentally double-booking with a training or another summit" implies no double-booking, BC-006 only one registration per day. Not conflict.
BC-045/046/047: summits details listing. similar no conflict.
BC-057/058: bulk approve sessions vs mark a session as accepted. similar no conflict.

Potential strong conflict:
- BC-006: "limit to one registration per day per authenticated user" (trainee wants limit to one registration per day). BC-038: "As attendee, register for a summit". If trainee and attendee roles? They may register for multiple trainings/summits same day? BC-040 says prevent double-booking with training or another summit. BC-006 one per day may conflict with registering for a summit and training on same day? But not explicitly. It says one registration per day per authenticated user, maybe a rule. BC-008 waitlist. BC-038 is summit registration, not training. Could be conflict if summit registration counts registration? Hmm.

- BC-011: "As a trainee, I want to add to 'my schedule' if there is a schedule feature on the site" conditional, not conflict.

- BC-013: "Trainers can see all class attendance at first because there are so little trainers and they are trusted with privacy" - "at first" may imply temporary, but not conflict.
- BC-014: admin view filtered. No conflict.
- BC-022: anonymous can see list attendees associated with company. This might conflict with privacy of user profiles? No.

Need check authentication/anonymous conflicts. Many stories assigned anonymoususer for actions that might require authenticated/account:
BC-033: As anonymoususer, sign up for newsletter. okay.
BC-059: As anonymoususer, receive notification when sessions evaluated. Anonymous can receive notification perhaps via email? But without account? They submitted session as anonymous? BC-062 anonymous register to speak; BC-060 anonymous receive notification when submit a session. Could be okay if email captured.
BC-062: As anonymoususer, register to speak. BC-063: As authenticateduser, submit a session. Potential conflict: one story says anonymous can register to speak/submit session; another says authenticateduser submits a session. This seems inconsistent: registration to speak/submission may require account. BC-062 says anonymoususer can register to speak, BC-063 says authenticateduser can submit a session. Could be two steps? BC-059 anonymous receive notification when sessions evaluated; BC-060 anonymous notification on submit. BC-061 authenticated edit session. Does BC-062 conflict with BC-063? Possibly not: BC-062 might be registration for speaker account, BC-063 actual submission after authentication.
